Nothing contained in this permit shall be construed to satisfy any legal obligations of the
permittee to comply with all applicable laws and regulations or to obtain any
governmental approval or permit from any entity other than the Agency, whether
federal, State, regional, or local.

This permit does not convey any right to trespass upon the lands or interfere with the
riparian rights of others in order to undertake the authorized project, nor does it authorize
the impairment of any easement, right, title or interest in real or personal property.

This authorization shall expire unless recorded in the Essex County Clerk's Office within
60 days of issuance of a signed and notarized permit. The signed and notarized permit
shall be recorded in the names of all persons listed above and in the names of all
owners of record of any portion of the project site on the recordation date.

This permit authorizes a two-lot subdivision in an area classified Moderate Intensity Use
on the Adirondack Park Land Use and Development Plan Map in the Town of
Ticonderoga, Essex County.
THIS IS A TWO-SIDED DOCUMENT

To the County Clerk: Please
index this permit in the grantor
index under the following name:
1. Scott M. Reale

The project shal be undertaken in compliance with all conditions stated herein. Failure
to comply with this permit is a violation and may subject the permittee, successors, and
assigns to civil penalties and other legal proceedings.
SUMMARY AND AUTHORIZATION
Date Issued: June 29, 2023

for a permit pursuant to S 809 of the Adirondack Park
Agency Act

The project shall not be undertaken or continued unless the project authorized herein is
in existence within five years of the date the permit is recorded in the Essex County
Clerk's Office. The Agency will consider the project in existence when the permit has
been recorded.

SCOTT M. REALE
Permittee
In the Matter of the Application of

The project site is a 1.05±-acre parcel of land located on Windy Point Way in the Town
of Ticonderoga, Essex County, in an area classified Moderate Intensity Use on the
Adirondack Park Land Use and Development Plan Map. The site is identified as Tax
Map Section 160.35, Block 1, Parcels 22.200, 25.000 and 26.000, and is described in a
deed from Nancy M. Reale to Nancy M. Reale as Trustee of the Nancy M. Reale
Revocable Living Trust, dated July 26, 2022, and recorded August 1, 2022 in the Essex
County Clerk's Office at Book 2092, Page 123.

Pursuant to Section 809(2)(a) of the Adirondack Park Agency Act, a permit is required
from the Adirondack Park Agency prior to any subdivision of Moderate Intensity Use
Iands that results in the creation of a shoreline lot smaller than O.57 acres in size in the
Adirondack Park.

The project is shown on a survey map titled "Map of a Lot Line Adjustment: Lands Now
or Formerly of Nancy M. Reale Revocable Living Trust,"prepared by Darrah Land
Surveying, PLLC, and dated February 14, 2023 (Site Plan). A reduced-scale copy of
the Site Plan is attached as a part of this permit for reference.

0.32±-acre lot containing an existing single family dweling and dock and a 0.73±-acre
lot containing an existing single family dwelling and boathouse.

The project site contains shoreline on Lake George, and is improved by two single
family dwellings, a dock, a boathouse and a shed.
AGENCY JURISDICTION

3.
In addition to complying with all terms and conditions of this permit, all future
activities on the project site shall be undertaken in compliance with the requirements
of New York State's Adirondack Park Agency Act, Freshwater Wetlands Act, and the
Adirondack Park Agency's implementing regulations [9 NYCRR SS 570-588].
Agency Permit 2023-0031
CONDITIONS
PROJECT DESCRIPTION
Page 2 of 4

The project shall not be undertaken until this permit has been recorded in the
Essex County Clerk's Office.

2.
This permit is binding on the permittee, all present and future owners or lessees
of the project site, and all persons undertaking all or a portion of the project.
Copies of this permit and the Site Plan shall be furnished by the permittee to all
subsequent owners or lessees of the project site prior to sale or lease, and by the
permittee and/or any subsequent owner or lessee to all persons undertaking any
development activities authorized herein.
PROJECT SITE
THE PROJECT IS APPROVED SUBJECT TO THE FOLLOWING CONDITIONS:

13.
There shall be no principal buildings located on the 0.32±-acre lot other than the
pre-existing single family dwelling or any replacement structure for this dwelling
as allowed by Agency regulations.

14.
There shall be no more than one principal building located on the 0.73±-acre lot
at any time. The single family dwelling constructed on the property in 1980
constitutes a principal building.

12.
The undertaking of any activity involving wetliands shall require a new or
amended permit.

4.
All deeds conveying all or a portion of the lands subject to this permit shall
contain references to this permit as follows: "The lands conveyed are subject to
Adirondack Park Agency Permit 2023-0031, issued June 29, 2023, the conditions
of which are binding upon the heirs, successors and assigns of the grantors and
all subsequent grantees."

Any deed of conveyance for the 0.32t-acre lot as depicted on the Site Plan shal
contain an easement providing access to the 0.73t-acre lot over the easement
area shown and described on the Site Plan.

10.
No structures greater than 100 square feet in size, shall be constructed within 50
feet, measured horizontally, of the mean high water mark of Lake George.
Agency Permit 2023-0031

11.
All wastewater treatment infrastructure on the project site shall be connected to
and served by the municipal wastewater treatment system.

8.
Any boathouse constructed on the project site must be used only for the storage
of boats and associated equipment, not contain sanitary plumbing of any kind,
and comply with the dimensional requirements established by the Lake George
Park Commission.

Prior to undertaking construction of any dock on the project site, written
authorization of plans for the dock, including all attached upland structures, shall
be obtained from the Agency.

Construction of any guest cottage on the project site shall require prior written
Agency authorization.

Subject to the conditions stated herein, this permit authorizes a two-lot
subdivision as depicted on the Site Plan. Any subdivision not depicted on the
Site Plan shall require prior written Agency authorization.

governmental approval or permit from any entity other than the Agency, whether
federal, State, regional, or local.

This permit does not convey any right to trespass upon the lands or interfere with the
riparian rights of others in order to undertake the authorized project, nor does it authorize
the impairment of any easement, right, title or interest in real or personal property.

This authorization shall expire unless recorded in the Essex County Clerk's Office within
60 days of issuance of a signed and notarized permit. The signed and notarized permit
shall be recorded in the names of all persons listed above and in the names of all
owners of record of any portion of the project site on the recordation date.

This permit authorizes a two-lot subdivision in an area classified Moderate Intensity Use
on the Adirondack Park Land Use and Development Plan Map in the Town of
Ticonderoga, Essex County.

index this permit in the grantor

1. Scott M. Reale

to comply with this permit is a violation and may subject the permittee, successors, and
assigns to civil penalties and other legal proceedings.
SUMMARY AND AUTHORIZATION
Date Issued: June 29, 2023

for a permit pursuant to S 809 of the Adirondack Park
Agency Act

The project shall not be undertaken or continued unless the project authorized herein is
in existence within five years of the date the permit is recorded in the Essex County
Clerk's Office. The Agency will consider the project in existence when the permit has
been recorded.

In the Matter of the Application of

The project site is a 1.05±-acre parcel of land located on Windy Point Way in the Town
of Ticonderoga, Essex County, in an area classified Moderate Intensity Use on the
Adirondack Park Land Use and Development Plan Map. The site is identified as Tax
Map Section 160.35, Block 1, Parcels 22.200, 25.000 and 26.000, and is described in a
deed from Nancy M. Reale to Nancy M. Reale as Trustee of the Nancy M. Reale
Revocable Living Trust, dated July 26, 2022, and recorded August 1, 2022 in the Essex
County Clerk's Office at Book 2092, Page 123.

Pursuant to Section 809(2)(a) of the Adirondack Park Agency Act, a permit is required
from the Adirondack Park Agency prior to any subdivision of Moderate Intensity Use
Iands that results in the creation of a shoreline lot smaller than O.57 acres in size in the
Adirondack Park.

The project is shown on a survey map titled "Map of a Lot Line Adjustment: Lands Now
or Formerly of Nancy M. Reale Revocable Living Trust,"prepared by Darrah Land
Surveying, PLLC, and dated February 14, 2023 (Site Plan). A reduced-scale copy of
the Site Plan is attached as a part of this permit for reference.

0.32±-acre lot containing an existing single family dweling and dock and a 0.73±-acre
lot containing an existing single family dwelling and boathouse.

The project site contains shoreline on Lake George, and is improved by two single
family dwellings, a dock, a boathouse and a shed.
AGENCY JURISDICTION

3.
In addition to complying with all terms and conditions of this permit, all future
activities on the project site shall be undertaken in compliance with the requirements
of New York State's Adirondack Park Agency Act, Freshwater Wetlands Act, and the
Adirondack Park Agency's implementing regulations [9 NYCRR SS 570-588].
Agency Permit 2023-0031

2.

Copies of this permit and the Site Plan shall be furnished by the permittee to all
subsequent owners or lessees of the project site prior to sale or lease, and by the
permittee and/or any subsequent owner or lessee to all persons undertaking any
development activities authorized herein.
PROJECT SITE
THE PROJECT IS APPROVED SUBJECT TO THE FOLLOWING CONDITIONS:

13.
There shall be no principal buildings located on the 0.32±-acre lot other than the
pre-existing single family dwelling or any replacement structure for this dwelling
as allowed by Agency regulations.

14.
There shall be no more than one principal building located on the 0.73±-acre lot
at any time. The single family dwelling constructed on the property in 1980
constitutes a principal building.

12.
The undertaking of any activity involving wetliands shall require a new or
amended permit.

4.
All deeds conveying all or a portion of the lands subject to this permit shall
contain references to this permit as follows: "The lands conveyed are subject to
Adirondack Park Agency Permit 2023-0031, issued June 29, 2023, the conditions
of which are binding upon the heirs, successors and assigns of the grantors and
all subsequent grantees."

Any deed of conveyance for the 0.32t-acre lot as depicted on the Site Plan shal
contain an easement providing access to the 0.73t-acre lot over the easement
area shown and described on the Site Plan.

10.
No structures greater than 100 square feet in size, shall be constructed within 50
feet, measured horizontally, of the mean high water mark of Lake George.
Agency Permit 2023-0031

11.
All wastewater treatment infrastructure on the project site shall be connected to
and served by the municipal wastewater treatment system.

8.
Any boathouse constructed on the project site must be used only for the storage
of boats and associated equipment, not contain sanitary plumbing of any kind,
and comply with the dimensional requirements established by the Lake George
Park Commission.

Prior to undertaking construction of any dock on the project site, written
authorization of plans for the dock, including all attached upland structures, shall
be obtained from the Agency.

Construction of any guest cottage on the project site shall require prior written
Agency authorization.

Subject to the conditions stated herein, this permit authorizes a two-lot
subdivision as depicted on the Site Plan. Any subdivision not depicted on the
Site Plan shall require prior written Agency authorization.

We understand that Idaho has long considered a property tax limit modeled
on California's Proposition 13, and dramatic increases in property values have
reignited debate on assessment/tax limits. But we implore you, do we really
want to be akin to California?
City of Payette ~ 700 Center Avefue ~ Payette, ID 83661 ~ 208-642-6024

Property tax systems are established by state legislation, yet the
overwhelming majority of property tax revenue supports local government.
Setting the proposed limits in SB 1021 thus represents a restriction by one
level of government, the state, on the funds available to another, local
jurisdictions.
RE: SB 1021
Dear Honorable Senate Committee Members:

Members of the Senate Committee
on Local Government and Taxation
January 27, 2021

The time has come to put a stop to the proposed harsh limits in SB 1021,
which will put severe pressure over time on local governments' ability to
deliver the services that their residents expect and need, from schools and
police and fire protection to city parks and affordable housing
initiatives. Local jurisdictions will be forced to increase fees for services such
as sewerage, trash pick-up, community college classes, and participation in
school athletics or other extracurricular activities. Like sales taxes, fees
typically fall hardest on those with the least ability to pay.

On behalf of the Citizens of Payette, we strongly urge you to vote against SB
1021.

Jeffrey f. Williams
Payette's Mayor

The limits proposed in SB 1021, are a deeply flawed means to counter rising
property taxes. They are offered in hope of reducing tax bills and slowing the shift in
tax burdens to residential property, but in fact they can result in higher taxes for the
very homeowners they are intended to assist and can cause unpredictable new
shifts in tax liabilities. Implementing the tax limits in SB 1021 will impose widely
differing tax obligations on owners of identical properties, reduce economic growth
by distorting taxpayer decision making, and greatly reduce the transparency and
accountability of the property tax system as a whole.

Not only will local jurisdictions be forced to cut services and increase fees, but this
bill will also severely hamstring our ability to foster economic development and
future growth. The best tax policy for our local jurisdictions seeking to grow our
economies are those that offer long-term certainty to businesses and individuals
and designed with the principles of efficiency, simplicity, and equity in mind. Smart
tax policies, which are not based on political whim such as SB 1021, also have the
best chance of promoting fairness across the board.
City of Payette ~ 700 Center Avenue ~ Payette, ID 83661 ~ 208-642-6024

Again, we respectfully urge you to keep Idaho prosperous and vote against SB 1021.
We do not want to be another California!
Sincerely,
CITY OF PAYETTE
January 22, 2021
Friday Legislative Update

This week saw the introduction of the property tax cap legislation that is sponsored by members of
the legislative Property Tax Working Group. Senate Bill 1021 would have a terrible impact on Idaho's
future economic growth and job creation, by forcing cities to tightly restrict residential and
commercial development, which is the engine of our state's economy and a primary revenue driver
for the sales and income taxes that fund state and local government. The bill is expected to be up for
a hearing in the Senate Local Government & Taxation Committee on Wednesday, January 27 or
Thursday, January 28 in the afternoon.

This week has been incredibly busy from the perspective of AIC staff having meetings, reviewing and
analyzing bills and working cooperatively with other local government association partners to
advocate before the Legislature.

By restricting local governments' ability to fund the services and infrastructure needed to serve
growth through the new construction levy, that tax burden will be shifted to current residents. If

The Legislature knows the answer to the problem and continues to refuse to pass legislation to raise
and/or index the homeowner's exemption or increase relief for elderly, disabled, widows and
disabled veterans through the circuit breaker.

The legislation is based on the disproved idea that local government property tax levies, not rapidly
rising residential values that are outstripping ag and commercial property values, are the policy
problem that needs addressed. As the Legislature has heard numerous times, even the property tax
freeze bill from last session would have still seen homeowners in rapidly growing areas paying more
in taxes because their property values are increasing so much faster than other classes of property.

For cities where new construction roll value constitutes less than 2% growth in the taxing district's
budget, the taxing district may choose either: (A) an increase including the highest dollar levy of the
previous three years, plus a growth factor for CPI that cannot exceed 3%, plus a growth factor
determined by applying the prior year's levy rate to the value of new construction and annexation
during the previous calendar year; or (B) the taxing district may choose a 3% increase.
Property Tax Cap: Senate Bill 1021

For cities that are growing, the property tax budget increase may be up to a maximum of 4% annually
(without voter approval for a temporary override of up to 2 years in duration with simple majority
voter approval or a permanent override approved by two-thirds of voters), plus: an increase including
the highest dollar levy of the previous three years, a growth factor for CPl that cannot exceed 3%, and
a growth factor determined by applying the prior year's levy rate to the value of new construction
and annexation during the previous calendar year, plus any forgone that the city chooses to capture.
The bill would make changes to the 3% Cap law as follows:

Legislation to divert $800,o00 from the State Liquor Account for funding the Peace Officers Standards
and Training Program (POsT) was introduced this week. House Bill 30, would split the amount equally
between the state and local governments. The AlC Board of Directors voted this week to oppose the
legislation because taking local government revenue, at a time when legislators are demanding that
cities provide property tax relief, will only add to the burden on city service funding. The state has a
massive revenue surplus that could have easily paid for this relatively small amount from the state
budget. Local governments were forced to the table to renegotiate the State Liquor Account
distribution formula during the Great Recession and local governments were forced to take a lower
share of future revenues as a result. AlC's lobbyists will be working this issue to let legislators know
of our opposition.

"Cities need to take a look at hitting the pause button on new development projects," said AIC
Legislative Chair Mayor John Evans of Garden City, "until we have a better understanding of the
impacts of this legislation. It would be irresponsible to allow development to happen that might
burden our existing property taxpayers with subsidizing new growth that they can't afford to pay."

as significant portions of state sales and income tax revenues are derived from construction and

We ask city officials to please contact their local legislators as soon as possible and respectfully ask
that they oppose Senate Bill 1021. Provide examples of development proposals that could be
affected and the economic impact to your community. Cities also need to work closely with
economic development agencies, chambers of commerce, building contractors, realtors and others to
advance the message about how devastating this legislation would be to Idaho's economy. AlC has
spoken with AGC, IBCA, the FOP, PFFI, Idaho Power, Simplot and many other organizations about the
potential harm to development and growth and welcomes your help in these important discussions.
Reach out to Legislators to Ask them to Oppose HB 16 on Disaster Emergencies

Another bill introduced this week would give the Idaho Legislature sweeping powers to modify or end
local disaster declarations made by cities and counties. House Bill 16 would be an unprecedented
state takeover of local disaster emergencies that are usually non-controversial and used to respond to
floods, mudslides, fires and other emergency situations. Please reach out to your legislators and let
them know that their locally elected city and county officials have been perfectly capable of managing
these situations without the state's involvement and that the unintended consequences and
potential loss of federal disaster funding is unacceptable.

4. DEVELOPMENT DESIRES: I would like to preserve the historical roots of the property by developing it
as The Brickyard residential subdivision. A local engineering firm and builder with extensive experience
has already agreed to work with me on the project to make this an attractive addition to the City of
Payette. Our preliminary estimates to fully develop the property into build ready lots is significant. But,
when completed it would be something we and the City of Payette should be proud of.

2. PRICE. The proposed minimum bid price in 2019 was $55,000.00. I don't know if that was for the
entire parcel, but if you are increasing the minimum bid price now and reducing the acreage, I would
suggest an opei bidaig process lstead oi seaied bids to ehtice Thore potehtial buyers to bid hore than
the minimum. This would of course benefit the City.

3. BIDDING PROCESS: As a potential buyer I would love to be the only one and offer the minimum bid if I
felt the price was very fair. In fact I did buy a lot from the City this way in 2019, but the city probably
could have attracted more potential buyers and a higher price if it had not been a sealed bid. But, to
offer more, someone would need to know exactly what they are buying and what others have offered
before deciding whether to offer more. I would suggest this for The Brickyard property and any future
property disposals as well. It would benefit the City in getting the best price and those bidding would be
fairly treated as well. You can set a final bid date, then post in the office and/or online the current
highest bid until the bid closes unless you have other criteria besides the highest bid.

1. DESCRIPTION OF PROPERTY. The proposed property is located at 1841 Decker Drive aka The
Brickyard, Payette, Idaho. The current parcel shown on the county map is over 11 acres, but contains
areas critical to the city for storm drainage and other uses. I've been told you are only going to sell 6
acres. For cost effective development of the property, please consider selling as much of the acreage as
possible to make it more attractive for development. There needs to be at least two ways to enter and
exit the property. So, either an easement to use Decker should be included, and/or you may want to
consider including the City owned parcel that exits to the east on Uehlin Drive.

We understand that Idaho has long considered a property tax limit modeled
on California's Proposition 13, and dramatic increases in property values have
reignited debate on assessment/tax limits. But we implore you, do we really
want to be akin to California?
City of Payette ~ 700 Center Avefue ~ Payette, ID 83661 ~ 208-642-6024

Property tax systems are established by state legislation, yet the
overwhelming majority of property tax revenue supports local government.
Setting the proposed limits in SB 1021 thus represents a restriction by one
level of government, the state, on the funds available to another, local
jurisdictions.
RE: SB 1021
Dear Honorable Senate Committee Members:

Members of the Senate Committee
on Local Government and Taxation
January 27, 2021

The time has come to put a stop to the proposed harsh limits in SB 1021,
which will put severe pressure over time on local governments' ability to
deliver the services that their residents expect and need, from schools and
police and fire protection to city parks and affordable housing
initiatives. Local jurisdictions will be forced to increase fees for services such
as sewerage, trash pick-up, community college classes, and participation in
school athletics or other extracurricular activities. Like sales taxes, fees
typically fall hardest on those with the least ability to pay.

On behalf of the Citizens of Payette, we strongly urge you to vote against SB
1021.

Jeffrey f. Williams
Payette's Mayor

The limits proposed in SB 1021, are a deeply flawed means to counter rising
property taxes. They are offered in hope of reducing tax bills and slowing the shift in
tax burdens to residential property, but in fact they can result in higher taxes for the
very homeowners they are intended to assist and can cause unpredictable new
shifts in tax liabilities. Implementing the tax limits in SB 1021 will impose widely
differing tax obligations on owners of identical properties, reduce economic growth
by distorting taxpayer decision making, and greatly reduce the transparency and
accountability of the property tax system as a whole.

Not only will local jurisdictions be forced to cut services and increase fees, but this
bill will also severely hamstring our ability to foster economic development and
future growth. The best tax policy for our local jurisdictions seeking to grow our
economies are those that offer long-term certainty to businesses and individuals
and designed with the principles of efficiency, simplicity, and equity in mind. Smart
tax policies, which are not based on political whim such as SB 1021, also have the
best chance of promoting fairness across the board.
City of Payette ~ 700 Center Avenue ~ Payette, ID 83661 ~ 208-642-6024

Again, we respectfully urge you to keep Idaho prosperous and vote against SB 1021.
We do not want to be another California!
Sincerely,

Friday Legislative Update

This week saw the introduction of the property tax cap legislation that is sponsored by members of
the legislative Property Tax Working Group. Senate Bill 1021 would have a terrible impact on Idaho's
future economic growth and job creation, by forcing cities to tightly restrict residential and
commercial development, which is the engine of our state's economy and a primary revenue driver
for the sales and income taxes that fund state and local government. The bill is expected to be up for
a hearing in the Senate Local Government & Taxation Committee on Wednesday, January 27 or
Thursday, January 28 in the afternoon.

This week has been incredibly busy from the perspective of AIC staff having meetings, reviewing and
analyzing bills and working cooperatively with other local government association partners to
advocate before the Legislature.

By restricting local governments' ability to fund the services and infrastructure needed to serve
growth through the new construction levy, that tax burden will be shifted to current residents. If

The Legislature knows the answer to the problem and continues to refuse to pass legislation to raise
and/or index the homeowner's exemption or increase relief for elderly, disabled, widows and
disabled veterans through the circuit breaker.

The legislation is based on the disproved idea that local government property tax levies, not rapidly
rising residential values that are outstripping ag and commercial property values, are the policy
problem that needs addressed. As the Legislature has heard numerous times, even the property tax
freeze bill from last session would have still seen homeowners in rapidly growing areas paying more
in taxes because their property values are increasing so much faster than other classes of property.

For cities where new construction roll value constitutes less than 2% growth in the taxing district's
budget, the taxing district may choose either: (A) an increase including the highest dollar levy of the
previous three years, plus a growth factor for CPI that cannot exceed 3%, plus a growth factor
determined by applying the prior year's levy rate to the value of new construction and annexation
during the previous calendar year; or (B) the taxing district may choose a 3% increase.

the highest dollar levy of the previous three years, a growth factor for CPl that cannot exceed 3%, and
a growth factor determined by applying the prior year's levy rate to the value of new construction
and annexation during the previous calendar year, plus any forgone that the city chooses to capture.

Legislation to divert $800,o00 from the State Liquor Account for funding the Peace Officers Standards
and Training Program (POsT) was introduced this week. House Bill 30, would split the amount equally
between the state and local governments. The AlC Board of Directors voted this week to oppose the
legislation because taking local government revenue, at a time when legislators are demanding that
cities provide property tax relief, will only add to the burden on city service funding. The state has a
massive revenue surplus that could have easily paid for this relatively small amount from the state
budget. Local governments were forced to the table to renegotiate the State Liquor Account
distribution formula during the Great Recession and local governments were forced to take a lower
share of future revenues as a result. AlC's lobbyists will be working this issue to let legislators know
of our opposition.

"Cities need to take a look at hitting the pause button on new development projects," said AIC
Legislative Chair Mayor John Evans of Garden City, "until we have a better understanding of the
impacts of this legislation. It would be irresponsible to allow development to happen that might
burden our existing property taxpayers with subsidizing new growth that they can't afford to pay."

4. DEVELOPMENT DESIRES: I would like to preserve the historical roots of the property by developing it
as The Brickyard residential subdivision. A local engineering firm and builder with extensive experience
has already agreed to work with me on the project to make this an attractive addition to the City of
Payette. Our preliminary estimates to fully develop the property into build ready lots is significant. But,
when completed it would be something we and the City of Payette should be proud of.

2. PRICE. The proposed minimum bid price in 2019 was $55,000.00. I don't know if that was for the
entire parcel, but if you are increasing the minimum bid price now and reducing the acreage, I would
suggest an opei bidaig process lstead oi seaied bids to ehtice Thore potehtial buyers to bid hore than
the minimum. This would of course benefit the City.

3. BIDDING PROCESS: As a potential buyer I would love to be the only one and offer the minimum bid if I
felt the price was very fair. In fact I did buy a lot from the City this way in 2019, but the city probably
could have attracted more potential buyers and a higher price if it had not been a sealed bid. But, to
offer more, someone would need to know exactly what they are buying and what others have offered
before deciding whether to offer more. I would suggest this for The Brickyard property and any future
property disposals as well. It would benefit the City in getting the best price and those bidding would be
fairly treated as well. You can set a final bid date, then post in the office and/or online the current
highest bid until the bid closes unless you have other criteria besides the highest bid.

1. DESCRIPTION OF PROPERTY. The proposed property is located at 1841 Decker Drive aka The
Brickyard, Payette, Idaho. The current parcel shown on the county map is over 11 acres, but contains
areas critical to the city for storm drainage and other uses. I've been told you are only going to sell 6
acres. For cost effective development of the property, please consider selling as much of the acreage as
possible to make it more attractive for development. There needs to be at least two ways to enter and
exit the property. So, either an easement to use Decker should be included, and/or you may want to
consider including the City owned parcel that exits to the east on Uehlin Drive.

Property tax systems are established by state legislation, yet the
overwhelming majority of property tax revenue supports local government.
Setting the proposed limits in SB 1021 thus represents a restriction by one
level of government, the state, on the funds available to another, local
jurisdictions.
RE: SB 1021
Dear Honorable Senate Committee Members:

Members of the Senate Committee
on Local Government and Taxation
January 27, 2021

The time has come to put a stop to the proposed harsh limits in SB 1021,
which will put severe pressure over time on local governments' ability to
deliver the services that their residents expect and need, from schools and
police and fire protection to city parks and affordable housing
initiatives. Local jurisdictions will be forced to increase fees for services such
as sewerage, trash pick-up, community college classes, and participation in
school athletics or other extracurricular activities. Like sales taxes, fees
typically fall hardest on those with the least ability to pay.

On behalf of the Citizens of Payette, we strongly urge you to vote against SB
1021.

Jeffrey f. Williams
Payette's Mayor

The limits proposed in SB 1021, are a deeply flawed means to counter rising
property taxes. They are offered in hope of reducing tax bills and slowing the shift in
tax burdens to residential property, but in fact they can result in higher taxes for the
very homeowners they are intended to assist and can cause unpredictable new
shifts in tax liabilities. Implementing the tax limits in SB 1021 will impose widely
differing tax obligations on owners of identical properties, reduce economic growth
by distorting taxpayer decision making, and greatly reduce the transparency and
accountability of the property tax system as a whole.

Not only will local jurisdictions be forced to cut services and increase fees, but this
bill will also severely hamstring our ability to foster economic development and
future growth. The best tax policy for our local jurisdictions seeking to grow our
economies are those that offer long-term certainty to businesses and individuals
and designed with the principles of efficiency, simplicity, and equity in mind. Smart
tax policies, which are not based on political whim such as SB 1021, also have the
best chance of promoting fairness across the board.

Again, we respectfully urge you to keep Idaho prosperous and vote against SB 1021.
We do not want to be another California!

This week saw the introduction of the property tax cap legislation that is sponsored by members of
the legislative Property Tax Working Group. Senate Bill 1021 would have a terrible impact on Idaho's
future economic growth and job creation, by forcing cities to tightly restrict residential and
commercial development, which is the engine of our state's economy and a primary revenue driver
for the sales and income taxes that fund state and local government. The bill is expected to be up for
a hearing in the Senate Local Government & Taxation Committee on Wednesday, January 27 or
Thursday, January 28 in the afternoon.

This week has been incredibly busy from the perspective of AIC staff having meetings, reviewing and
analyzing bills and working cooperatively with other local government association partners to
advocate before the Legislature.

By restricting local governments' ability to fund the services and infrastructure needed to serve
growth through the new construction levy, that tax burden will be shifted to current residents. If

The Legislature knows the answer to the problem and continues to refuse to pass legislation to raise
and/or index the homeowner's exemption or increase relief for elderly, disabled, widows and
disabled veterans through the circuit breaker.

The legislation is based on the disproved idea that local government property tax levies, not rapidly
rising residential values that are outstripping ag and commercial property values, are the policy
problem that needs addressed. As the Legislature has heard numerous times, even the property tax
freeze bill from last session would have still seen homeowners in rapidly growing areas paying more
in taxes because their property values are increasing so much faster than other classes of property.

during the previous calendar year; or (B) the taxing district may choose a 3% increase.

Legislation to divert $800,o00 from the State Liquor Account for funding the Peace Officers Standards
and Training Program (POsT) was introduced this week. House Bill 30, would split the amount equally
between the state and local governments. The AlC Board of Directors voted this week to oppose the
legislation because taking local government revenue, at a time when legislators are demanding that
cities provide property tax relief, will only add to the burden on city service funding. The state has a
massive revenue surplus that could have easily paid for this relatively small amount from the state
budget. Local governments were forced to the table to renegotiate the State Liquor Account
distribution formula during the Great Recession and local governments were forced to take a lower

Galena Consulting has over twenty years' experience in directing planning processes for agencies
in the public sector:

Our specific experience in strategic, operations, and capital planning for local governments
throughout the West ensures Payette will receive a strategic plan that reflects the policy
objectives of the elected officials, department leaders, community members and other
stakeholders.

Our specific experience conducting Payette's 2009 and 2016 strategic planning processes,
and developing impact fees for the City of Payette gives us a unique perspective on the needs
of the City.

Our specific experience in local government budget development and analysis ensures that
the Payette will receive a strategic plan that is reflective of the fiscal realities of the
community, and identifies the budget initiatives and/or alternatives that must be included in

Introduction

Galena Consulting is uniquely qualified to facilitate a strategic planning process for the City of
Payette that clearly identifies the City's mission, goals, and objectives; aligns with the City's
annual budget planning processes; and sets forth specific action steps for the realization of the
City's goals and objectives.

Our specific experience in work planning and performance management ensures Payette will
receive a strategic plan that is actionable and measurable — clearly defining the steps that will
be taken by each department to realize the City's vision over a defined period of time.

Payette is a unique organization which supports a unique city. Rather than the application of a
template, this plan will be flexible and responsive to the distinctive needs of the City.

with elected officials and staff (3-4 hours) informed by the information gathering and public
involvement phases of the project. This will be followed by an action planning work session
with elected officials and staff (3-4 hours) to develop specific action steps necessary to
achieve the desired goals and objectives set forth in the strategic planning session.

Galena Consulting can begin to facilitate the update of Payette's strategic plan in February 2021.
The actual timeline of the proposed scope of work will depend on the availability of elected
officials and staff.

adoption of the strategic plan by the Mayor and City Council Members.

2016 Strategic Plan and gather additional information about the City's current condition to
enhance the planning process. Specific attention will be spent evaluating current facilities
and services, and future service delivery needs.

process through a survey of community members to determine their concerns and priorities
for the City of Payette. Surveys would be conducted in an electronic format, collecting
data anonymously. This survey tool could be repeated at a later date as a benchmark to
determine the progress being made within the Strategic Action Plan. *Alternatively, or in
addition, Consultant can conduct a community open house to gather public input.

4. DEVELOPMENT DESIRES: I would like to preserve the historical roots of the property by developing it
as The Brickyard residential subdivision. A local engineering firm and builder with extensive experience
has already agreed to work with me on the project to make this an attractive addition to the City of
Payette. Our preliminary estimates to fully develop the property into build ready lots is significant. But,
when completed it would be something we and the City of Payette should be proud of.

2. PRICE. The proposed minimum bid price in 2019 was $55,000.00. I don't know if that was for the
entire parcel, but if you are increasing the minimum bid price now and reducing the acreage, I would
suggest an opei bidaig process lstead oi seaied bids to ehtice Thore potehtial buyers to bid hore than
the minimum. This would of course benefit the City.

3. BIDDING PROCESS: As a potential buyer I would love to be the only one and offer the minimum bid if I
felt the price was very fair. In fact I did buy a lot from the City this way in 2019, but the city probably
could have attracted more potential buyers and a higher price if it had not been a sealed bid. But, to
offer more, someone would need to know exactly what they are buying and what others have offered
before deciding whether to offer more. I would suggest this for The Brickyard property and any future
property disposals as well. It would benefit the City in getting the best price and those bidding would be
fairly treated as well. You can set a final bid date, then post in the office and/or online the current
highest bid until the bid closes unless you have other criteria besides the highest bid.

1. DESCRIPTION OF PROPERTY. The proposed property is located at 1841 Decker Drive aka The
Brickyard, Payette, Idaho. The current parcel shown on the county map is over 11 acres, but contains
areas critical to the city for storm drainage and other uses. I've been told you are only going to sell 6
acres. For cost effective development of the property, please consider selling as much of the acreage as
possible to make it more attractive for development. There needs to be at least two ways to enter and
exit the property. So, either an easement to use Decker should be included, and/or you may want to
consider including the City owned parcel that exits to the east on Uehlin Drive.

Respectfully.

The purpose of this Mlemorandum is to address the drainage of Ridge West No. 4 Subdivision existing Lot
S8 proposed Lot 67. The property is located at approximately 750 North 950 West Circle. There is an area
of prior grading disturbance within the 3o% slope category. The owner intends to build a retaining wall
not to exceed 8 feet in height, approximately 5 feet into the existing 3o% hillside area and flatten the
disturbed area into a buildable backyard area. We also proposed seeding the downslope of the disturbed
area for improved hydrologic conditions.

No grading is being proposed on the new Lot 67. The slopes in this lot are in the 29% or less category. It
slopes down to the existing improved public right-of-way of 9so West Circle. The adjacent church has
landscaped the proposed lot and the natural grade of the lot is serving as a small drainage basin. Because
no changes are being proposed on Lot 67 and because the uphill disturbance will be brought to a better
condition, the existing drainage study should govern the undisturbed Lot 67. We proposed that no
changes occur to Lot 67 until the home building permit is requested for the property. Existing storm drain
Inlets and improvements in 95o West Circle currently accommodate dralnage runoff conditions and as we
are proposing no changes to existing drainage conditions on Lot 67 and proposing improved drainage
conditions on Lot 58.

the applicant is proposing to change the zone to allow for a multifamily development. This

The proposal is to build 19 multifamily units. This averages out to 15 units per acre. Each unit will

feet of amenities. The Redhawk development also has access to the Grayhawk amenities and has
been approved for short-term rentals. Redhawk has 19 units which requires 3,800 square feet of
amenity space. Redhawk has not been built yet, but it does have 5,204 square feet of recreational
space that includes a gazebo and green space. Silverhawk will have 19 units as well and is

Respectfully.

The purpose of this Mlemorandum is to address the drainage of Ridge West No. 4 Subdivision existing Lot
S8 proposed Lot 67. The property is located at approximately 750 North 950 West Circle. There is an area
of prior grading disturbance within the 3o% slope category. The owner intends to build a retaining wall
not to exceed 8 feet in height, approximately 5 feet into the existing 3o% hillside area and flatten the
disturbed area into a buildable backyard area. We also proposed seeding the downslope of the disturbed
area for improved hydrologic conditions.

No grading is being proposed on the new Lot 67. The slopes in this lot are in the 29% or less category. It
slopes down to the existing improved public right-of-way of 9so West Circle. The adjacent church has
landscaped the proposed lot and the natural grade of the lot is serving as a small drainage basin. Because
no changes are being proposed on Lot 67 and because the uphill disturbance will be brought to a better
condition, the existing drainage study should govern the undisturbed Lot 67. We proposed that no
changes occur to Lot 67 until the home building permit is requested for the property. Existing storm drain
Inlets and improvements in 95o West Circle currently accommodate dralnage runoff conditions and as we
are proposing no changes to existing drainage conditions on Lot 67 and proposing improved drainage
conditions on Lot 58.

Grayhawk has 244 units which requires 48,800 square feet of amenities. They have 49,406 square
feet of amenities. The Redhawk development also has access to the Grayhawk amenities and has
been approved for short-term rentals. Redhawk has 19 units which requires 3,800 square feet of
amenity space. Redhawk has not been built yet, but it does have 5,204 square feet of recreational

pool, clubhouse, and playground area which satisfies the requirements for short-term rentals.

Respectfully.

The purpose of this Mlemorandum is to address the drainage of Ridge West No. 4 Subdivision existing Lot
S8 proposed Lot 67. The property is located at approximately 750 North 950 West Circle. There is an area
of prior grading disturbance within the 3o% slope category. The owner intends to build a retaining wall
not to exceed 8 feet in height, approximately 5 feet into the existing 3o% hillside area and flatten the
disturbed area into a buildable backyard area. We also proposed seeding the downslope of the disturbed
area for improved hydrologic conditions.

No grading is being proposed on the new Lot 67. The slopes in this lot are in the 29% or less category. It
slopes down to the existing improved public right-of-way of 9so West Circle. The adjacent church has
landscaped the proposed lot and the natural grade of the lot is serving as a small drainage basin. Because
no changes are being proposed on Lot 67 and because the uphill disturbance will be brought to a better
condition, the existing drainage study should govern the undisturbed Lot 67. We proposed that no
changes occur to Lot 67 until the home building permit is requested for the property. Existing storm drain
Inlets and improvements in 95o West Circle currently accommodate dralnage runoff conditions and as we
are proposing no changes to existing drainage conditions on Lot 67 and proposing improved drainage
conditions on Lot 58.

feels, at this time, this location is not conducive to commercial or office development. Therefore,
the applicant is proposing to change the zone to allow for a multifamily development. This
development is to be called Silverhawk and will be owned and managed by the same company

have 2 bedroom and 2.5 baths with an attached two-car garage and will be built similar to the

feet of amenities. The Redhawk development also has access to the Grayhawk amenities and has
been approved for short-term rentals. Redhawk has 19 units which requires 3,800 square feet of
amenity space. Redhawk has not been built yet, but it does have 5,204 square feet of recreational
space that includes a gazebo and green space. Silverhawk will have 19 units as well and is

Given the design and operational requirements for a municipal solid waste transfer station and in
part the site constraints posed by the existing salt barns, we believe it is necessary and
appropriate to extend the road network into Parcel C. As such, MWA requests the BOA consider
expanding the existing Special Use Permit (allowing a solid waste transfer station on Lot 6) to
include allowing a solid waste transfer station on Parcel C. On October 18, 2013 MWA began
the re-zoning process for Parcel C to change the zoning from A-1 to M-3 with the submission of
a request for a Waiver of Requirements to allow M-3 use within the Highway 141 Mixed Use
Development Corridor District.

It should also be noted that transfer tractor-trailers will enter the lower level "load-out area" of
the transfer station building from the east. This will allow the transfer trailers to directly exit the
site to the west after being loaded with waste. To safely and efficiently accommodate this
transfer tractor-trailer loading operation, access is through the right-of-way easement onto Parcel
C. This transfer tractor-trailer roadway on Parcel C will also connect to the egress roads from
the maneuvering and small vehicle areas.

waste transfer station on Parcel C and looks forward to working with the City of Grimes on this

Metro Northwest Transfer Station

Site access will be controlled and limited to a time when a transfer station operator who has met
the proper training requirements is on duty. The training requirements include the reading,
understanding, and implementation of this document and the reading, understanding, and
implementation of the ERRAP. This also includes the ability to visually recognize universal
symbols and markings, and indications of unacceptable materials pursuant to subrule 106.1 1(4). In
addition, the operations manager shall also be certified by a training program approved by the
Department such as, but not limited to, the Solid Waste Association of North America's Managing
Transfer Station Systems Training and Certification Course since the facility will be permitted for
20,000 tons or more per year of solid waste. A copy of facility operator certificate for Metro
Waste Authority's (MWA) operations manager is included in Section E. See Section D for
MW A's organizational chart.

Tires and white goods incidental to acceptance of solid waste during public events may be
unloaded and transferred outside of the transfer station facility. These materials are typically
transferred into transportation vehicles and removed from the site the day of the event.
Metro Northwest Transfer Station

To the extent practical, transfer station operators will segregate and manage identifiable
unacceptable wastes and hot loads in accordance with applicable laws and in a safe and
responsible manner. Due to the nature of the operation, the operator typically pushes each load
after it has been dumped on the tip floor. Therefore, the load is observed and if unacceptable
wastes are observed they are immediately segregated. The solid waste hauler responsible for
leaving the waste is then notified to retrieve it from the transfer station.
2018 Permit Application

The transfer station operator, at a minimum, visually inspects all solid waste accepted by the
transfer station for hot loads and hazardous, infectious, radioactive, and other wastes not accepted
for disposal in a sanitary landfill.

the waste stream, stored outside of the transfer building, and periodically removed from the site.
SEGREGATION AND MANAGEMENT OF UnACCEPTABLE WASTES

Solid waste is only accepted that is generated in MW A's service area. Delivery is typically
restricted to approved waste haulers with the exception of public vehicles allowed for periodic
public events held on designated Saturdays.

2018 Permit Application

Transfer station operators are currently not allowed to salvage materials, although this practice is
allowed under the code and may be changed at some future date. However, scavenging is
prohibited.

Although the receipt of a hot load is not expected to occur often, any hot load will typically be
isolated from the other waste in the transfer station, wetted down with water, and allowed to cool
until it is no longer a fire hazard. A load inspection form is completed and placed on file on site
documenting unacceptable waste and hot loads.
October 2018
Metro Northwest Transfer Station

Vectors and vermin are controlled by removing solid waste from the building, by using regular
insecticide spray schedules, bait traps, and by regular washing of floors, equipment, and other
areas of the building as required. The practice of "first-in" is "first-out' for waste handling reduces
time solid waste is present at the facility. Putrescible loads will be given priority in loading so as
to reduce the time they are present on site and to reduce odors.

Section H- Site Operation Plan

Unloading, handling, and transferring solid waste inside the transfer building limits the generation
of litter. During each day of operation, litter will be picked up from the outside of the transfer
building on an as-needed basis. Litter fences will be utilized near the tunnel. Periodic cleaning will
prevent litter accumulation inside the building.

106.11(6)

Routine operational maintenance of the facility will be conducted in an adequate manner.

I rench drains win be installed in the floor of the transfer station, in the Iower Tevel tunnel, and
beneath the load-out scales (See Attachment G-4). These drains will be connected to a grease and
grit trap and the sanitary sewer system and serve to collect wash water and other liquids. Periodic
inspection, cleaning, and repairs of the trench drains will be performed to maintain proper
operation conditions. If repairs are needed, surfaces in waste handling and wash-down areas will
not be used for waste handling unless the area is repaired to maintain a surface impermeable to
liquids. Repairs to any breach of an impervious surface will be performed within 24 hours of
discovery of the breach.

106.11(13)
ROUTINE OPERATIONAL MAInTENANCE

Transfer station trailers are power washed off-site, as necessary to control odor, excessive mud,
vectors, and vermin. Equipment to be used within the transfer building is easily cleaned. Wash
water will be collected and will drain to the grease and grit trap and will then be pumped to the
sanitary sewer system. The tipping floor within the transfer station will be cleaned as needed to
prevent a nuisance or public health hazard.

The hazardous substance has the potential to reach any surface water or groundwater.

The hazardous substance has the potential to leave the property by flowing over the
surface or through sewers, tile lines, culverts, drains, utility lines, or some other conduit.

"Hazardous substance"means any substance or mixture of substances that presents a
danger to the public health or safety and includes, but is not limited to, a substance that is toxic,
corrosive, or flammable, or that is an irritant or that, in confinement, generates pressure through
decomposition, heat, or other means. The following are examples of substances which, in sufficient
quantity, may be hazardous: acids; alkalis; explosives; fertilizers; heavy metals such as chromium,
arsenic, mercury, lead and cadmium; industrial chemicals; paint thinners; paints; pesticides;
petroleum products; poisons; radioactive materials; sludges; and organic solvents. "Hazardous
substances" may include any hazardous waste identified or listed by the administrator of the United
States Environmental Protection Agency under the Solid Waste Disposal Act as amended by the
Resource Conservation and Recovery Act of 1976, or any toxic pollutant listed under Section 307 of
the federal Water Pollution Control Act as amended to January 1, 1977, or any hazardous substance
designated under Section 311 of the federal Water Pollution Control Act as amended to January 1,
1977, or any hazardous material designated by the secretary of transportation under the Hazardous
Materials Transportation Act (49 CFR S172.101).

567—131.2(455B) Report of hazardous conditions. Any person manufacturing. storing. handling.
transporting, or disposing of a hazardous substance shall notify the department at (515)281-8694
and the local police department or the office of the sheriff of the affected county of the occurrence of
a hazardous condition as soon as possible but not later than six hours after the onset of the
hazardous condition or discovery of the hazardous condition. A sheriff or police chief who has been
notified of a hazardous condition shall immediately notify the department. Reports made pursuant to
this rule shall be confirmed in writing as provided in 131.2(2).

IAC 7/2/08 Environmental Protection[567] Ch 131, p.1
CHAPTER 131
NOTIFICATION OF HAZARDOUS CONDITIONS

"Corrosive"means causing or producing visible destruction or irreversible alterations in
human skin tissue at the site of contact, or in the case of leakage of a hazardous substance from its
packaging, causing or producing a severe destruction or erosion of other materials through chemical
processes.

131.2(2) Written report. The written report of such a hazardous condition shall be submitted
to the department within 3o days and contain the following information:
a. The exact location of the hazardous condition.
b. The time and date of onset or discovery of the hazardous condition.

"Hazardous condition"means any situation involving the actual, imminent or probable
spillage, leakage, or release of a hazardous substance onto the land, into a water of the state or into
the atmosphere which, because of the quantity, strength and toxicity of the hazardous substance, its
mobility in the environment and its persistence, creates an immediate or potential danger to the
public health or safety or to the environment.

Metro Waste Authority (MW A) Northwest Transfer Station will consist of three parcels of land
owned by MW A. , Lot 6, Parcel C and Parcel D, located at 4105 SE Beisser Drive within the City
of Grimes, Iowa. In conjunction with purchasing Lot 6, MWA received a Special Use Permit for
the transfer station dated November 5, 1998 from the City of Grimes Board of Adjustment. Lot 6
was zoned M-3 (Heavy Industrial) at the time of purchase. On December 17, 2013, the Grimes
Board of Adjustment approved MW A's request for a Special Use Permit for solid waste transfer
Requirements for Hwy 141 Corridor. Parcel D lies entirely within a dedicated roadway right-of-
way (ROW). MWA is utilizing its rights to this ROW easement to access MW A's property.
MWA's purchase of this property simply shifts the maintenance of this parcel of ROW from its
prior owner to MW A. Copies of the following documents are attached:

In accordance with the City of Grimes Ordinances, Chapter 165, Section 165.37 Special Permits,
Metro Waste Authority (MWA) hereby requests the City of Grimes Board of Adjustment (BOA)
to consider expanding an existing Special Use Permit (Appeal No. 05-98) dated November 5,
1998 for a proposed municipal solid waste transfer station to be located at 4105 SE Beisser
Drive. The existing Special Use Permit applies to one of two parcels owned by Metro Waste
Authority. Please find attached a BOA application, conceptual site plan, and copy of existing
Special Use Permit for the proposed municipal solid waste transfer station.

Given the design and operational requirements for a municipal solid waste transfer station and in
part the site constraints posed by the existing salt barns, we believe it is necessary and
appropriate to extend the road network into Parcel C. As such, MWA requests the BOA consider
expanding the existing Special Use Permit (allowing a solid waste transfer station on Lot 6) to
include allowing a solid waste transfer station on Parcel C. On October 18, 2013 MWA began
the re-zoning process for Parcel C to change the zoning from A-1 to M-3 with the submission of
a request for a Waiver of Requirements to allow M-3 use within the Highway 141 Mixed Use
Development Corridor District.

It should also be noted that transfer tractor-trailers will enter the lower level "load-out area" of
the transfer station building from the east. This will allow the transfer trailers to directly exit the
site to the west after being loaded with waste. To safely and efficiently accommodate this
transfer tractor-trailer loading operation, access is through the right-of-way easement onto Parcel
C. This transfer tractor-trailer roadway on Parcel C will also connect to the egress roads from
the maneuvering and small vehicle areas.

MWA request the Board of Adjustment expands the existing Special Use Permit to allow a solid
waste transfer station on Parcel C and looks forward to working with the City of Grimes on this
project. I would encourage you to schedule a tour of our existing facility located on Delaware
Avenue if you would like to see first hand the type of facility that is being proposed. If you
should require any additional information or have any questions or concerns, please feel free to
contact me at (515) 323-6535.

litter generation at the site.

in the floor of the transfer station (see Attachment G-4 for the design plans). Floor drains will also
be installed in the lower level tunnel and beneath the load-out scale(s). These drains will be
connected to the sanitary sewer system and will serve to collect wash water and other liquids.

during construction of this project.

approximately 0.414 acres of wetlands will be permanently impacted by this project. 0.322 acres

Mitigation Bank at a 2:1 ratio for permanent impacts (O.84 acres). For temporary impacts, the
site will be restored to pre-construction contours following the relocation of the sewer line.

Engineers a copy of the Proof of Purchase from the Voas Wetland Mitigation Bank.

Metro Northwest Transfer Station

Site access will be controlled and limited to a time when a transfer station operator who has met
the proper training requirements is on duty. The training requirements include the reading,
understanding, and implementation of this document and the reading, understanding, and
implementation of the ERRAP. This also includes the ability to visually recognize universal
symbols and markings, and indications of unacceptable materials pursuant to subrule 106.1 1(4). In
addition, the operations manager shall also be certified by a training program approved by the
Department such as, but not limited to, the Solid Waste Association of North America's Managing
Transfer Station Systems Training and Certification Course since the facility will be permitted for
20,000 tons or more per year of solid waste. A copy of facility operator certificate for Metro
Waste Authority's (MWA) operations manager is included in Section E. See Section D for
MW A's organizational chart.

Tires and white goods incidental to acceptance of solid waste during public events may be
unloaded and transferred outside of the transfer station facility. These materials are typically
transferred into transportation vehicles and removed from the site the day of the event.
Metro Northwest Transfer Station

To the extent practical, transfer station operators will segregate and manage identifiable
unacceptable wastes and hot loads in accordance with applicable laws and in a safe and
responsible manner. Due to the nature of the operation, the operator typically pushes each load
after it has been dumped on the tip floor. Therefore, the load is observed and if unacceptable
wastes are observed they are immediately segregated. The solid waste hauler responsible for
leaving the waste is then notified to retrieve it from the transfer station.
2018 Permit Application

The transfer station operator, at a minimum, visually inspects all solid waste accepted by the
transfer station for hot loads and hazardous, infectious, radioactive, and other wastes not accepted
for disposal in a sanitary landfill.

Solid waste is only accepted that is generated in MW A's service area. Delivery is typically
restricted to approved waste haulers with the exception of public vehicles allowed for periodic
public events held on designated Saturdays.

2018 Permit Application

Transfer station operators are currently not allowed to salvage materials, although this practice is
allowed under the code and may be changed at some future date. However, scavenging is
prohibited.

Although the receipt of a hot load is not expected to occur often, any hot load will typically be
isolated from the other waste in the transfer station, wetted down with water, and allowed to cool
until it is no longer a fire hazard. A load inspection form is completed and placed on file on site
documenting unacceptable waste and hot loads.
October 2018
Metro Northwest Transfer Station

Vectors and vermin are controlled by removing solid waste from the building, by using regular
insecticide spray schedules, bait traps, and by regular washing of floors, equipment, and other
areas of the building as required. The practice of "first-in" is "first-out' for waste handling reduces
time solid waste is present at the facility. Putrescible loads will be given priority in loading so as
to reduce the time they are present on site and to reduce odors.

Section H- Site Operation Plan

Unloading, handling, and transferring solid waste inside the transfer building limits the generation
of litter. During each day of operation, litter will be picked up from the outside of the transfer
building on an as-needed basis. Litter fences will be utilized near the tunnel. Periodic cleaning will
prevent litter accumulation inside the building.

106.11(6)
SCAVENGING
Routine operational maintenance of the facility will be conducted in an adequate manner.

I rench drains win be installed in the floor of the transfer station, in the Iower Tevel tunnel, and
beneath the load-out scales (See Attachment G-4). These drains will be connected to a grease and
grit trap and the sanitary sewer system and serve to collect wash water and other liquids. Periodic
inspection, cleaning, and repairs of the trench drains will be performed to maintain proper
operation conditions. If repairs are needed, surfaces in waste handling and wash-down areas will
not be used for waste handling unless the area is repaired to maintain a surface impermeable to
liquids. Repairs to any breach of an impervious surface will be performed within 24 hours of
discovery of the breach.

106.11(13)
ROUTINE OPERATIONAL MAInTENANCE

Transfer station trailers are power washed off-site, as necessary to control odor, excessive mud,
vectors, and vermin. Equipment to be used within the transfer building is easily cleaned. Wash
water will be collected and will drain to the grease and grit trap and will then be pumped to the
sanitary sewer system. The tipping floor within the transfer station will be cleaned as needed to
prevent a nuisance or public health hazard.

The transfer station will be inspected annually by an Iowa-licensed professional engineer (P.E.).
The inspection, at a minimum, covers the design standards pursuant to rule IAC 567
106.10(455B). The inspection report will reflect the facility's compliance with respect to the
Department-approved design and construction. The annual engineering inspection report will be
submitted to the Department by the first workday in November each year.
Section H - Site Operation Plan
Metro Northwest Transfer Station

The portion of the solid waste transport vehicle that contains solid waste will be suficient to
prevent the accidental discharge of its contents, the attraction or harborage of vectors, and
infiltration of precipitation. Transport vehicles with an open top will have a suitable cover, which
is not easily torn, shredded, broken, or breached under normal use.

Transfer station vehicles will be cleaned at intervals frequent enough to prevent a nuisance or
vector attraction. Wastewater generated from the cleaning of the areas of the solid waste transport
vehicles that hold solid waste are considered washwater and is managed accordingly.

The hazardous substance has the potential to leave the property by flowing over the

"Hazardous substance"means any substance or mixture of substances that presents a
danger to the public health or safety and includes, but is not limited to, a substance that is toxic,
corrosive, or flammable, or that is an irritant or that, in confinement, generates pressure through
decomposition, heat, or other means. The following are examples of substances which, in sufficient
quantity, may be hazardous: acids; alkalis; explosives; fertilizers; heavy metals such as chromium,
arsenic, mercury, lead and cadmium; industrial chemicals; paint thinners; paints; pesticides;
petroleum products; poisons; radioactive materials; sludges; and organic solvents. "Hazardous
substances" may include any hazardous waste identified or listed by the administrator of the United
States Environmental Protection Agency under the Solid Waste Disposal Act as amended by the
Resource Conservation and Recovery Act of 1976, or any toxic pollutant listed under Section 307 of
the federal Water Pollution Control Act as amended to January 1, 1977, or any hazardous substance
designated under Section 311 of the federal Water Pollution Control Act as amended to January 1,
1977, or any hazardous material designated by the secretary of transportation under the Hazardous
Materials Transportation Act (49 CFR S172.101).

567—131.2(455B) Report of hazardous conditions. Any person manufacturing. storing. handling.
transporting, or disposing of a hazardous substance shall notify the department at (515)281-8694
and the local police department or the office of the sheriff of the affected county of the occurrence of
a hazardous condition as soon as possible but not later than six hours after the onset of the
hazardous condition or discovery of the hazardous condition. A sheriff or police chief who has been
notified of a hazardous condition shall immediately notify the department. Reports made pursuant to
this rule shall be confirmed in writing as provided in 131.2(2).

IAC 7/2/08 Environmental Protection[567] Ch 131, p.1
CHAPTER 131
NOTIFICATION OF HAZARDOUS CONDITIONS

"Corrosive"means causing or producing visible destruction or irreversible alterations in
human skin tissue at the site of contact, or in the case of leakage of a hazardous substance from its
packaging, causing or producing a severe destruction or erosion of other materials through chemical
processes.

131.2(2) Written report. The written report of such a hazardous condition shall be submitted
to the department within 3o days and contain the following information:
a. The exact location of the hazardous condition.
b. The time and date of onset or discovery of the hazardous condition.

"Hazardous condition"means any situation involving the actual, imminent or probable
spillage, leakage, or release of a hazardous substance onto the land, into a water of the state or into
the atmosphere which, because of the quantity, strength and toxicity of the hazardous substance, its
mobility in the environment and its persistence, creates an immediate or potential danger to the
public health or safety or to the environment.

Metro Waste Authority (MW A) Northwest Transfer Station will consist of three parcels of land
owned by MW A. , Lot 6, Parcel C and Parcel D, located at 4105 SE Beisser Drive within the City
of Grimes, Iowa. In conjunction with purchasing Lot 6, MWA received a Special Use Permit for
the transfer station dated November 5, 1998 from the City of Grimes Board of Adjustment. Lot 6
was zoned M-3 (Heavy Industrial) at the time of purchase. On December 17, 2013, the Grimes
Board of Adjustment approved MW A's request for a Special Use Permit for solid waste transfer
Requirements for Hwy 141 Corridor. Parcel D lies entirely within a dedicated roadway right-of-
way (ROW). MWA is utilizing its rights to this ROW easement to access MW A's property.

DearMr. McAreavy:
October 31, 2013

In accordance with the City of Grimes Ordinances, Chapter 165, Section 165.37 Special Permits,
Metro Waste Authority (MWA) hereby requests the City of Grimes Board of Adjustment (BOA)
to consider expanding an existing Special Use Permit (Appeal No. 05-98) dated November 5,
1998 for a proposed municipal solid waste transfer station to be located at 4105 SE Beisser
Drive. The existing Special Use Permit applies to one of two parcels owned by Metro Waste
Authority. Please find attached a BOA application, conceptual site plan, and copy of existing
Special Use Permit for the proposed municipal solid waste transfer station.

Given the design and operational requirements for a municipal solid waste transfer station and in
part the site constraints posed by the existing salt barns, we believe it is necessary and
appropriate to extend the road network into Parcel C. As such, MWA requests the BOA consider
expanding the existing Special Use Permit (allowing a solid waste transfer station on Lot 6) to
include allowing a solid waste transfer station on Parcel C. On October 18, 2013 MWA began
the re-zoning process for Parcel C to change the zoning from A-1 to M-3 with the submission of
a request for a Waiver of Requirements to allow M-3 use within the Highway 141 Mixed Use
Development Corridor District.

It should also be noted that transfer tractor-trailers will enter the lower level "load-out area" of
the transfer station building from the east. This will allow the transfer trailers to directly exit the
site to the west after being loaded with waste. To safely and efficiently accommodate this
transfer tractor-trailer loading operation, access is through the right-of-way easement onto Parcel
C. This transfer tractor-trailer roadway on Parcel C will also connect to the egress roads from
the maneuvering and small vehicle areas.

connected to the sanitary sewer system and will serve to collect wash water and other liquids.

Your project is covered under Nationwide Permit No. 39, as published in the enclosed
Federal Register(77 FR 10184)on February 21,2012, provided you meet the permit conditions
for the nationwide permits which are included in the Federal Register. You must also comply
with the special conditions listed below. The Corps has also made a determination of no effect
on federally threatened and endangered species or critical habitat. The Iowa Department of
Natural Resources (IADNR) has also issued Section 401 Water Quality Certification with
conditions for this nationwide permit. The decision regarding this action is based on information
found in the administrative record, which documients the District's decision-making process, the
basis for the decision, and the final decision.

2. Bank and shoreline protection shall consist of suitable clean materials, free from debris,
trash, and other deleterious materials. If broken concrete is used asriprap, all reinforcing rods
must be cut flush with the surface of the concrete, and individual pieces of concrete shall not
exceed 3 feet in any dimension. Asphalt, car bodies, and broken concrete containing asphalt are
specifically excluded from this authorization.

1. You are encouraged to conduct your construction activities during a period of low flow.
You are required to remove al fill material used as a temporary crossing, causeway, or work pad
to an upland, non-wetland site, to seed al disturbed areas with native grasses, and to implement
appropriate measures to insure that sediments are not introduced into waters of the United States
during construction of this project.

Based on your application and follow up discussions with HDR, it has been deternined that
approximately 0.414 acres of wetlands will be permanently impacted by this project. 0.322 acres
of wetlands will be temporarily impacted bythe relocation of a storm sewer. To compensate for
these losses, wetland mitigation will consist of purchasing credits from the Voas Wetland
Mitigation Bank at a 2:1 ratio for permanent impacts (O.84 acres). For temporary impacts, the
site will be restored to pre-construction contours following the relocation of the sewer line.
Within 30 days of placing fill into the wetland, Metro Waste Authority will provide the Corps of
Engineers a copy of the Proof of Purchase from the Voas Wetland Mitigation Bank.

DEPARTMENT OF THE ARMY
CORPS OF ENGINEERS, ROCK ISLAND DISTRICT

Section 17, Township 79North,Range 25 West, Polk County, Iowa.
