Dear Mr. Dworek:

3. Polk County is within the known breeding range of the federally endangered Indiana Bat
(Myotis sodalis). The Corps has made a determination of not likely to adversely affect federally
threatened and endangered species provided no habitat or potential habitat for listed species will
be impacted by the project. If habitat may be afected, then further coordination with the US
Fish and Wildlife Servicewill be necessary.

The Rock Island District Regulatory Branch is committed to providing quality and timely
service to our customers. In an effort to improve customer service, please take a moment to
complete the attached postcard and return it or go to our Customer Service Survey found on our
web site at http://per2.nwp.usace.army.mil/survey.html.(Be sure to select"Rock Island District"
under the area entitled: Which Corps office did you deal with?)

You are required to complete and return the enclosed "Completed Work Certification" form
upon completion of your project in accordance with General Condition No. 30 of the nationwide
permits.
Sincerely,

4. Metro Waste will provide the Corps of Engineers a pre and post construction survey of
the wetlands that will be temporarily impacted. The purpose of this survey will be to show that
the wetlands are returned to their pre-construction state. The post construction survey will also
serve as the one required report. This report will list the species planted and their location.

Our office has completed a Preliminary Jurisdictional Determination concerning your project
area. It was mailed to you September 16, 2013.

5. Within 30 days of placing fill into the wetland, Metro Waste Authority will provide the
Corps of Engineers a copy of the Proof of Purchase showing that 0.84 acres of wetland credit
were purchased.

This verification is valid until March 18, 2017, unless the nationwide permit is modified,
reissued or revoked. It is your responsibility to remain informed of changes to the nationwide
permit program. We will issue a public notice announcing any changes if and when they occur.
Furthermore, if you commence or are under contract to commence this activity before the date
the nationwide permit is modified or revoked, you will have twelve months from that date to
compete your activity under the present terms and conditions of this nationwide permit.

Should you have any questions, please contact our Regulatory Branch by letter, or telephone
me at 309/794-5859.

Albert J. Frohlich

Metro Northwest Transfer Station

Site access will be controlled and limited to a time when a transfer station operator who has met
the proper training requirements is on duty. The training requirements include the reading,
understanding, and implementation of this document and the reading, understanding, and
implementation of the ERRAP. This also includes the ability to visually recognize universal
symbols and markings, and indications of unacceptable materials pursuant to subrule 106.1 1(4). In
addition, the operations manager shall also be certified by a training program approved by the
Department such as, but not limited to, the Solid Waste Association of North America's Managing
Transfer Station Systems Training and Certification Course since the facility will be permitted for
20,000 tons or more per year of solid waste. A copy of facility operator certificate for Metro
Waste Authority's (MWA) operations manager is included in Section E. See Section D for
MW A's organizational chart.

Tires and white goods incidental to acceptance of solid waste during public events may be
unloaded and transferred outside of the transfer station facility. These materials are typically
transferred into transportation vehicles and removed from the site the day of the event.
Metro Northwest Transfer Station

To the extent practical, transfer station operators will segregate and manage identifiable
unacceptable wastes and hot loads in accordance with applicable laws and in a safe and
responsible manner. Due to the nature of the operation, the operator typically pushes each load
after it has been dumped on the tip floor. Therefore, the load is observed and if unacceptable
wastes are observed they are immediately segregated. The solid waste hauler responsible for
leaving the waste is then notified to retrieve it from the transfer station.
2018 Permit Application

The transfer station operator, at a minimum, visually inspects all solid waste accepted by the
transfer station for hot loads and hazardous, infectious, radioactive, and other wastes not accepted
for disposal in a sanitary landfill.
October 2018

TRANSFER STATION OPERATING REQUIREMENTS [IAC 567 106.11]

Tires, white goods and residential collection carts found in the haulers' loads are separated from
the waste stream, stored outside of the transfer building, and periodically removed from the site.
SEGREGATION AND MANAGEMENT OF UnACCEPTABLE WASTES

Solid waste is only accepted that is generated in MW A's service area. Delivery is typically
restricted to approved waste haulers with the exception of public vehicles allowed for periodic
public events held on designated Saturdays.
SECTION H: SITE OPERATION PLAN [IAC 567 106.8(1)"k"]

106.11(4)
VISUAL INSPECTION
2018 Permit Application

Transfer station operators are currently not allowed to salvage materials, although this practice is
allowed under the code and may be changed at some future date. However, scavenging is
prohibited.

Although the receipt of a hot load is not expected to occur often, any hot load will typically be
isolated from the other waste in the transfer station, wetted down with water, and allowed to cool
until it is no longer a fire hazard. A load inspection form is completed and placed on file on site
documenting unacceptable waste and hot loads.
October 2018
Metro Northwest Transfer Station

Vectors and vermin are controlled by removing solid waste from the building, by using regular
insecticide spray schedules, bait traps, and by regular washing of floors, equipment, and other
areas of the building as required. The practice of "first-in" is "first-out' for waste handling reduces
time solid waste is present at the facility. Putrescible loads will be given priority in loading so as
to reduce the time they are present on site and to reduce odors.

106.11(8,10)

106.11(11,12)

Section H- Site Operation Plan

Unloading, handling, and transferring solid waste inside the transfer building limits the generation
of litter. During each day of operation, litter will be picked up from the outside of the transfer
building on an as-needed basis. Litter fences will be utilized near the tunnel. Periodic cleaning will
prevent litter accumulation inside the building.

106.11(6)
SCAVENGING
Routine operational maintenance of the facility will be conducted in an adequate manner.

I rench drains win be installed in the floor of the transfer station, in the Iower Tevel tunnel, and
beneath the load-out scales (See Attachment G-4). These drains will be connected to a grease and
grit trap and the sanitary sewer system and serve to collect wash water and other liquids. Periodic
inspection, cleaning, and repairs of the trench drains will be performed to maintain proper
operation conditions. If repairs are needed, surfaces in waste handling and wash-down areas will
not be used for waste handling unless the area is repaired to maintain a surface impermeable to
liquids. Repairs to any breach of an impervious surface will be performed within 24 hours of
discovery of the breach.

106.11(13)
ROUTINE OPERATIONAL MAInTENANCE

Transfer station trailers are power washed off-site, as necessary to control odor, excessive mud,
vectors, and vermin. Equipment to be used within the transfer building is easily cleaned. Wash
water will be collected and will drain to the grease and grit trap and will then be pumped to the
sanitary sewer system. The tipping floor within the transfer station will be cleaned as needed to
prevent a nuisance or public health hazard.

The Metro Northwest Transfer Station will have approximately 16,000 square feet of tipping floor

IDNR GUIDELINES FOR REPORTING HAzARDOUS
CONDITIONS INCLUDING CHAPTER 131
IOWA ADMINISTRATIVE CODE "NOTIFICATION OF
HAZARDOUS CONDITIONS"
ATTACHMENT D

It is recommended that all spills be cleaned up although a particular spill may not be reportable.
A series of small spills over the years can result in one big cleanup!
Department rules stress the immediate or potential danger that a spill may cause.
In general, lowa reporting requirements are more stringent than Federal reporting requirements.
However, the time limit for reporting at the Federal level is more immediate.

Compliance & Enforcement Bureau
Iowa Department of Natural Resources
Telephone: 515/725-0387, e-mail:rodney.tucker@dnr.iowa.gov

Lee, Kathleen

You should report a spill now if:

conditions. Liaison to local, state, and federal emergency planning groups.
Telephone: 515/725-0384, e-mail: kathy.lee@dnr.iowa.gov

Provides 24-hour technical assistance and regulatory oversight regarding spills and hazardous
conditions. Liaison to local, state, and federal emergency planning groups.
Tucker, Rodney

Broughton, Adam

The hazardous substance can be detected in the air at the boundaries of the facility
property by the senses (sight and smell) or by monitoring equipment.

If you need to report a spill, or have any questions about the need to report,
call (515) 281-8694 or contact our Emergency Response Unit.

Provides 24-hour technical assistance and regulatory oversight regarding spills and hazardous
conditions. Liaison to local, state, and federal emergency planning groups.
Telephone: 515/725-0386, e-mail:adam.broughton@dnr.iowa.gov
The hazardous substance has the potential to reach any surface water or groundwater.

The hazardous substance has the potential to leave the property by flowing over the
surface or through sewers, tile lines, culverts, drains, utility lines, or some other conduit.

"Hazardous substance"means any substance or mixture of substances that presents a
danger to the public health or safety and includes, but is not limited to, a substance that is toxic,
corrosive, or flammable, or that is an irritant or that, in confinement, generates pressure through
decomposition, heat, or other means. The following are examples of substances which, in sufficient
quantity, may be hazardous: acids; alkalis; explosives; fertilizers; heavy metals such as chromium,
arsenic, mercury, lead and cadmium; industrial chemicals; paint thinners; paints; pesticides;
petroleum products; poisons; radioactive materials; sludges; and organic solvents. "Hazardous
substances" may include any hazardous waste identified or listed by the administrator of the United
States Environmental Protection Agency under the Solid Waste Disposal Act as amended by the
Resource Conservation and Recovery Act of 1976, or any toxic pollutant listed under Section 307 of
the federal Water Pollution Control Act as amended to January 1, 1977, or any hazardous substance
designated under Section 311 of the federal Water Pollution Control Act as amended to January 1,
1977, or any hazardous material designated by the secretary of transportation under the Hazardous
Materials Transportation Act (49 CFR S172.101).

567—131.2(455B) Report of hazardous conditions. Any person manufacturing. storing. handling.
transporting, or disposing of a hazardous substance shall notify the department at (515)281-8694
and the local police department or the office of the sheriff of the affected county of the occurrence of
a hazardous condition as soon as possible but not later than six hours after the onset of the
hazardous condition or discovery of the hazardous condition. A sheriff or police chief who has been
notified of a hazardous condition shall immediately notify the department. Reports made pursuant to
this rule shall be confirmed in writing as provided in 131.2(2).

IAC 7/2/08 Environmental Protection[567] Ch 131, p.1
CHAPTER 131
NOTIFICATION OF HAZARDOUS CONDITIONS

"Corrosive"means causing or producing visible destruction or irreversible alterations in
human skin tissue at the site of contact, or in the case of leakage of a hazardous substance from its
packaging, causing or producing a severe destruction or erosion of other materials through chemical
processes.

131.2(2) Written report. The written report of such a hazardous condition shall be submitted
to the department within 3o days and contain the following information:
a. The exact location of the hazardous condition.
b. The time and date of onset or discovery of the hazardous condition.

"Hazardous condition"means any situation involving the actual, imminent or probable
spillage, leakage, or release of a hazardous substance onto the land, into a water of the state or into
the atmosphere which, because of the quantity, strength and toxicity of the hazardous substance, its
mobility in the environment and its persistence, creates an immediate or potential danger to the
public health or safety or to the environment.

[Prior to 7/1/83, DEQ Ch 41]

"Irritant"means a substance causing or producing dangerous or intensely irritating fumes
upon contact with fire or when exposed to air.
567—131.1(455B) Definitions. For purposes of this chapter:

131.2(1) Verbal report. The verbal report of such a hazardous condition should provide
information on as many items listed in 131.2(2) as available data will allow.
Environmental Protection[567] IAC

"Toxic"means causing or producing a dangerous physiological, anatomic or biochemical
change in a biological system.

131.2(3) Reporting of subsequent findings. All subsequent finding and laboratory results
should be reported and submitted in writing to the department as soon as they become available.
These rules are intended to implement lowa Code section 455B.115.
